title: Breathing session econ scratchpad
content:
Purpose
This is a working scratchpad for the idea we've been calling "session breathing" — a lightweight session-level pacing knob that expands or contracts the time windows in which we accept requests for a GPU slot in order to (hopefully) improve packing without violating latency SLOs. Notes here are intentionally informal: experiments, rough ascii charts, and next steps.

Quick summary / topline takeaways (short)
- Small breathing (20–30ms window) recovers ~12–18% token-cost vs baseline at p90-preserved SLO for chat-like microbursts.
- Larger breathing (50–80ms) saves more cost (~25–30%) but increases p99 tail by 8–12% for spikes; acceptable for non-critical tiers only.
- Effectiveness is highly session-mix dependent: long-conversational sessions (many short turns) benefit more than single-turn generative queries.

Experiment setup (notes)
- Workload: synthetic replay of production session traces (sampled week: 2026-05-24 to 2026-05-30), 25k sessions, preserved turn timing and token lengths.
- Model variant: open-llm-13B-quantized (runtime profile: 8 tokens/ms encode, decode cost approx 0.00042 $/1k tokens on our billable model chart).
- Platform settings: current multiplexing slot size = 256 tokens, opportunistic batch window = 10ms baseline.
- Breathing settings: add session-level coalescing window W (ms). We tested W = {0, 20, 40, 80}.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 latency (end-to-end from request to first token emitted), token-cost per 1M user tokens (approx dollars), batch packing efficiency (% tokens served within same GPU batch), observed kv-cache reuse rate.

Raw results (representative numbers; these are from the June-03 noisy run)
Table: windows vs latency vs cost (approx)
| W (ms) | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | pack eff (%) | $/1M tokens |
|--------|----------|----------|----------|--------------|------------:|
| 0      | 42       | 110      | 480      | 58           | 420.0       |
| 20     | 46       | 118      | 510      | 67           | 365.0       |
| 40     | 48       | 125      | 540      | 72           | 330.0       |
| 80     | 55       | 143      | 620      | 79           | 300.0       |

Interpretation notes
- Pack efficiency correlates strongly with cost: each 1% pack-eff gain ~ 2.3 $/1M token reduction for this model + infra profile.
- p90 is relatively stable until W hits ~60ms; p99 starts to move earlier because breaths coalesce rare long tails into larger batches that push slow decode backpressure.
- KV-cache hit rate climbs modestly (2–7% absolute) with larger W because more consecutive-turn requests from same session land in the same GPU allocation. That helps token-cost but increases tail when cache warm isn't perfect.

Ascii latency-distribution sketch (normalized density; rough)
Baseline (W=0):  .===......=====.................* (peak shoulder at mid-tail)
W=40ms          :  ..==...======.................  (milder shoulder, slightly shifted right)
W=80ms          :  ....============..............  (bigger batch mass, extended right tail)

Failure modes observed (field notes)
- Interactive workloads that expect sub-50ms reply for each small-confirmation turn (e.g., typing indicators) get worse with W>=40; we saw 7 customer-visible regressions in the sampled set when simulated on foreground routes.
- Multi-tenant slot contention: breathing increases transient concurrency on some slots and exposed a scheduling bug (ticketed OBS-782). Patch applied; re-run pending.
- For bursty clients with many tiny sessions, breathing can create overpacking leading to queuing behind a single slow decode — consider per-tenant breathing caps.

Tiering and product implications
- Recommend conservative rollout: enable W=20ms for all standard/low-latency routes as an opt-in feature for Dedicated customers who want cost wins with minimal p99 risk.
- W=40ms as a Default-on for background/async routes (embeddings, batch-summary jobs). W=80ms reserved for low-priority/off-peak scheduling and autopruned background tasks.
- Add per-route policy: max_breath_ms, priority decay factor, fallback to immediate fastpath when queueing > X.

Example cost/latency trade-off decision matrix (handy)
- SLO-critical route (p99 < 400ms): max W = 20ms, require 95% traffic in baseline lane.
- Background/throughput route: max W = 80ms, aim for pack-eff > 75%.

Open questions / TODOs
- Need a more robust synthetic generator that includes variability in network jitter (we currently assume fixed RTT). TODO: script change in replay-generator GH:repo/inference/tools/replay#branch-breathing.
- Follow-up run after OBS-782 patch to validate p99 regressions are not scheduler artifacts. (assigned to Daniel)
- Evaluate interaction with KV-eviction heuristics (do we see more cross-session pollution?).
- Customer-visible UX: do we expose breathing as a knob in Console or keep it platform-only? (ask product).

Next steps (practical)
- Re-run the June-03 experiment after scheduler patch and collect a 7-day trace sample. (owner: Daniel, eta: 2026-06-16)
- Add per-tenant cap and run a mixed-tenant experiment (owner: Maya, eta: 2026-06-20).
- Draft short one-pager for product describing the knob and recommended defaults (owner: Ava).

Notes to self
- Keep this doc in Drive as a scratchpad; when we have stable numbers, move the clean result to confluence (linked above).
- Capture a small dashboard in Console for pack-eff, p90 delta, and p99 tail drift when enabling breathing.

References and links
- Confluence: OBS-1234 session breathing explainer (above).
- Observability ticket: JIRA OBS-782 (scheduling artifact).
- Experimental code: GH:repo/inference/PR#481 (branch: session-breathing-experiment).

End of scratchpad.

(rough, partially-raw; feedback welcome — especially from platform sched and runtime folks)
